newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares extend New Year's bull run.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares extend New Year's bull run.

text.p: Chilean stocks climbed nearly a full point on strong foreign buying and another upgrade for Chile from an overseas brokerage.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended 0.92 percent higher at 108.81 points. The all-share IGPA rose 0.51 percent to close at 5160.08 points on slow volume of 8.2 billion pesos.

The market was betting slower economic growth and cuts in government spending would soon bring a reduction in interest rates, but the main force behind the bolsas bull run was still an influx of foreign buying, analysts said.

''We think the market is rising more because of purchases by institutional investors who think shares are undervalued,'' rather than on speculation about a rate cut, said Ida Longeri, senior analyst at brokers Larrain Vial.

But shares will fall a bit if an expected easing of interest rates fails to materalize, said Longeri. Her brokerage wasn't expecting any rate cut until February but wouldn't rule out one earlier, she said.
Oppenheimer nudged up Chile in a Latin American equity report to market weight from underperform, the latest in a flurry of upgrades.
Reports like Oppenheimer's may not set the market tone but they do ''make the rises that have already occurred more sustainable,'' said Longeri.
The IPSA fell 17 percent in real terms last year, despite seven percent economic growth, leaving the bolsa ready for an upswing early this year, said brokers.
''The market is betting on a rate cut, no doubt about it, but there's also strong reliance on foreign investors and domestic optimism that the market's tendency is changing,'' said one broker.
Madeco rose 0.5 percent to 1090 pesos. The company said it would post sharply higher revenues this year thanks to purchase of Brazilian firm Ficap.
High-volume electrical shares were mostly higher. Endesa was up 2.1 percent to 239.80 pesos and Enersis lifted 0.8 percent to 248 pesos.
Decliners included Laboratorio Chile, retreating from recent gains and losing 1.6 percent to 368 pesos, and Cruz Blanca, off 1.5 percent to 130 pesos.
Banco Santiago preferred stock B series slipped 2.9 percent to 10.20 pesos. The bank just merged with Banco O'Higgins and has taken over O'Higgins' ticker symbol OHG.N.
